canonical_id.description: Unique identifier for the dataset across versions in a project
canonical_id.decided_by: A stable id from the source system (LIMS id, accession, run id). Together with `version` and `project` it is the record's signature, so it must come out identical on every re-run.
canonical_id.common_mistakes: Building it from values that change between runs (timestamps, temp paths), which mints a new record every run. Composite ids out of order or `_`-joined: order the parts highest to lowest granularity and join with `/`, the same way for every record.

version.description: Version string for the dataset (defaults to '1.0.0')
version.decided_by: The source's own release or version label; `1.0.0` when it has none.
version.common_mistakes: Passing `null`: the field is a string, so send `1.0.0` rather than nothing.

project.description: Initiative that this dataset belongs to ex: CellXGene, SRA, CryoET, Shrimp, DynaCell
project.decided_by: The initiative the data belongs to. Part of the signature.
project.common_mistakes: Using a lab or person name. Use the initiative name other records in that initiative already use (check with search facets).

modality.description: Data modality (imaging, sequencing, mass spec, text, or unknown)
modality.decided_by: The acquisition technology, derived from the assay or file format rather than copied verbatim from a source column.

governance.common_mistakes: Putting access, consent, or compliance values that have no named field here (e.g. `consent`, `data_use_agreement`). The block accepts extra keys, but only the named fields are governance; put the rest under `metadata.additional_metadata`.

governance.license.description: License under which the dataset is made available. This can either be the name of the license like 'MIT' or a link to the term of agreement
governance.license.decided_by: The data owner or the source's terms. Ask; never infer.
governance.license.common_mistakes: Guessing a license because the dataset is public somewhere.

examples.note: a URL to bespoke terms also works

governance.data_sensitivity.description: Classification level of data sensitivity: 'Low', 'Medium' or 'High'
governance.data_sensitivity.decided_by: Leave unset. Records registered through this plugin do not populate it.
governance.data_sensitivity.common_mistakes: Mapping a source sensitivity column onto it, or routing it to custom metadata instead.

governance.access_scope.description: Gates record visibility: exactly 'internal' (the server default) or 'public'
governance.access_scope.decided_by: Always `internal` for records registered through this plugin. Never mapped from a source field.

governance.is_pii.description: Required. Whether the dataset contains Personally Identifiable Information. 'I am not sure' is not False — ask your data steward before you write
governance.is_pii.decided_by: Consent and data source, confirmed by a person who knows them. Never inferred from file contents.
governance.is_pii.common_mistakes: Defaulting to `false` because the field is required. `false` is a claim, not a default.

examples.note: commercial cell line, no donor data (confirmed by the data owner)

governance.is_phi.description: Required. Whether the dataset contains Protected Health Information
governance.is_phi.decided_by: Consent and data source, confirmed by a person who knows them. Never inferred from file contents.
governance.is_phi.common_mistakes: Defaulting to `false` because the field is required, or treating it as the same question as `is_pii`.

governance.data_steward.description: Required. Person or org that defines the standards and best practices for the data's accuracy, quality and completeness, and ingests and formats datasets to meet them
governance.data_steward.decided_by: Ask the user. There is no honest empty value.
governance.data_steward.common_mistakes: Substituting `data_owner` or a contact address. Steward and owner are different accountabilities.

governance.data_generator.type: string or list of string, nullable
governance.data_generator.description: Person, lab or org that produced the data. Pass a list when more than one party generated it

governance.data_owner.description: Person or organization that owns the data
governance.data_owner.common_mistakes: Inventing one when the source has none; leave it unset.

governance.is_external_reference.description: Whether this dataset references external data hosted by a third part, and not stored locally

governance.embargoed_until.description: Date until which the dataset is under embargo/restricted access

metadata.description: Biological, experimental and data quality metadata

metadata.experiment.sub_modality.description: Specific sub-type within the main data modality

metadata.experiment.assay[].label.description: Human-readable name or label for the ontology term

metadata.experiment.assay[].ontology_id.description: Unique identifier from the relevant ontology (e.g., GO:0001234, NCBI:9606)
metadata.experiment.assay[].ontology_id.decided_by: An ontology lookup that matches the label exactly (case-insensitive, label or synonym). Leave unset when there is no confident match.
metadata.experiment.assay[].ontology_id.common_mistakes: Naming the key `ontology_term_id`; it is `ontology_id`. Fabricating or partially guessing a CURIE.

metadata.experiment.machine_information.description: Information about instruments or machines used

metadata.experiment.experimental_protoco.description: Protocols and procedures used in the experiment

metadata.sample.description: Biological sample characteristics and preparation metadata

metadata.sample.organism.description: Organism(s) from which the sample was derived
metadata.sample.organism.common_mistakes: Deriving it from a cell type that exists in several species. Fill it from another column only when that column uniquely determines it (a cell line pins its species), and confirm the rule with the user first.

metadata.sample.organism[].label.description: Human-readable name or label for the ontology term

metadata.sample.organism[].ontology_id.description: Unique identifier from the relevant ontology (e.g., GO:0001234, NCBI:9606)

metadata.sample.tissue.description: Tissue(s) from which the sample was derived
metadata.sample.tissue.common_mistakes: Adding a separate `cell_line` key instead of a tissue entry with `type: cell line`. Naming the key `tissue_type`; it is `type`.

examples.note: cell lines go here, with `type: cell line`

metadata.sample.tissue[].label.description: Human-readable name or label for the ontology term

metadata.sample.tissue[].ontology_id.description: Unique identifier from the relevant ontology (e.g., GO:0001234, NCBI:9606)

metadata.sample.tissue[].type.description: Additional tissue type classification (e.g., 'organelle', 'cell line', 'tissue', 'cell culture', 'organoid')

metadata.sample.development_stage[].labe.description: Human-readable name or label for the ontology term

metadata.sample.development_stage[].onto.description: Unique identifier from the relevant ontology (e.g., GO:0001234, NCBI:9606)

metadata.sample.disease.description: Disease(s) or pathological condition(s) associated with the sample

metadata.sample.disease[].label.description: Human-readable name or label for the ontology term

metadata.sample.disease[].ontology_id.description: Unique identifier from the relevant ontology (e.g., GO:0001234, NCBI:9606)

metadata.sample.perturbation.description: Codebook of the distinct perturbations applied, one entry per perturbation with 'id', 'type' (chemical/protein/genetic/environmental/combination/none/other/unknown) and 'role' (treatment/negative_control/positive_control/untreated). Per-cell or per-well assignment stays in the data, keyed by 'id'. Stored unvalidated

metadata.sample.sample_parent.description: Information about the parent sample or source

metadata.sample.sample_preparation_proto.description: Protocols used for sample preparation and processing

metadata.data_summary.description: Summary statistics and characteristics of the data

metadata.data_summary.cell_count.description: Total number of cells detected or segmented in the dataset
metadata.data_summary.cell_count.common_mistakes: Copying a collection-level total onto every dataset in it.

metadata.data_summary.read_count.description: Number of reads or sequences (for sequencing data)

metadata.data_summary.read_length.description: Length of reads in base pairs (for sequencing data)

metadata.data_summary.read_confidence.description: Quality score or confidence measure for reads

metadata.data_summary.observation_unit.description: Sequencing and imaging. What one observation represents. Leave unset where observations are not the unit, such as FASTQs

metadata.data_summary.is_combined.description: All modalities. True when the data combines more than one data acquisition; combining files from a single acquisition does not count. Unset means unknown, so a search for False returns only datasets explicitly marked single-acquisition

metadata.data_summary.axes.description: OME-ngff v0.5 axes metadata; length MUST equal the number of array dimensions; each entry has 'name', 'type', and 'unit' keys; units MUST follow OME-ngff v0.5 specification for spatial and temporal dimensions

metadata.data_summary.channels.description: DCA per-channel metadata array (dca.channels); SHOULD include an entry for each channel in the image
metadata.data_summary.channels.common_mistakes: Leaving out a channel: include one entry per channel in the image's C axis, with `index` matching its position.

metadata.data_summary.channels[].name.description: Short name capturing the acquisition and/or biological context (e.g. 'H2B-GFP', 'Phase2D'); SHOULD match the OME-NGFF omero.channels label

metadata.data_summary.channels[].index.description: Zero-based channel index in the C axis

metadata.data_summary.channels[].descrip.description: Rich natural language description of the channel suitable for text embedding; SHOULD capture biological target and imaging context

metadata.data_summary.channels[].channel.description: Functional type of the channel; SHOULD be one of: fluorescence (fluorescent label microscopy), chromogenic (chromogenic staining e.g. H&E, IHC), labelfree (brightfield, phase, DIC), predicted (computationally predicted via virtual staining)

metadata.data_summary.channels[].biologi.description: Biological target details for the channel; SHOULD be provided for fluorescence and predicted channels
Target organelle, structure, or protein class visualized (e.g. 'chaperones', 'actin filament', 'nuclei')

Type of reagent used to label the target; SHOULD be one of: endogenous_tag (genetically encoded fluorescent protein), live_cell_dye (cell-permeable dye applied to living cells), fixed_dye (dye applied after fixation), antibody (fluorescently conjugated antibody). SHOULD be provided for fluorescent channels.
Specific reagent, protein, or dye used (e.g. 'HSPA1B', 'FastAct_SPY555 Live Cell Dye', 'virtual stain')

metadata.data_summary.resolution.description: Spatial and temporal resolution of the imaging data using OME-ngff v0.5 units

metadata.data_summary.resolution.spatial.description: Spatial resolution per axis using OME-ngff v0.5 units (e.g., {'x': 0.1, 'y': 0.1, 'z': 0.25, 'unit': 'micrometer'})

metadata.data_summary.resolution.tempora.description: Temporal resolution using OME-ngff v0.5 units (e.g., {'interval': 5, 'unit': 'second'})

metadata.data_summary.dimension.description: Shape of the 5D image array in (time, channels, z, y, x) order; all datasets MUST be 5-dimensional with placeholder values where a dimension is unused

metadata.data_summary.multiscales.description: OME-ngff v0.5 multiscales metadata stored in zarr.json at the group level; includes pyramid levels, coordinate transforms, and MUST document the downsampling method used

metadata.data_summary.plate.description: Plate metadata for OME-ngff v0.5 HCS layout; SHOULD follow OME-ngff 0.5 standards for high-content screening datasets

metadata.data_summary.well.description: Well metadata for OME-ngff v0.5 HCS layout; SHOULD follow OME-ngff 0.5 standards for high-content screening datasets

metadata.data_summary.fov.description: Field-of-view level identifier in an OME-ngff HCS layout (e.g. plate.ome.zarr/A/3/0); the level at which DCA metadata (dca key) is stored in zarr.json

metadata.data_summary.channel_normalizat.description: Per-channel normalization statistics stored in dca.normalization_statistics; keyed by zero-based channel index (as string); used for display scaling and AI model training normalization
Intensity statistics computed over all spatial dimensions and timepoints for that channel; MUST be present for each channel normalization entry
Wide robust range: 99th percentile minus 1st percentile
Per-timepoint intensity statistics keyed by zero-based timepoint index (as string); if present, MUST contain entries for all timepoints in the dataset

description.common_mistakes: Repeating the name. Say what was measured, on what, and how.

doi.description: Digital Object Identifier for the dataset

cross_db_references.type: list of string or string, nullable
cross_db_references.description: References to external databases or systems

dataset_type.description: Whether dataset is raw or processed
dataset_type.decided_by: Processing stage: instrument output is `raw`; anything a pipeline produced from it is `processed`; derived results such as embeddings or statistics are `analysis`.

is_latest.description: Whether this is the latest version of the dataset

record_schema_version.description: Version of the record schema used for this dataset
record_schema_version.decided_by: The client model. Never set it by hand.
record_schema_version.common_mistakes: Mapping a source field onto it.

metadata_schema.description: Schema version used for the metadata structure

data_quality.description: Results of data quality validation checks

data_quality.checks_passed.description: List of data quality checks that passed validation
data_quality.checks_passed.meaning: Quality checks that passed. Items may be any shape (names, counts, objects); state the evidence for each.

data_quality.checks_failed.description: List of data quality checks that failed validation

data_quality.checks_skipped.description: List of data quality checks that were skipped or not applicable

data_quality.report_assets.description: Human-readable QC reports, one entry per file, as {'name': ..., 'uri': ...} (e.g. {'name': 'fastqc', 'uri': 's3://bucket/qc/fastqc.html'}). Pointers only; the catalog never fetches or hosts them

data_quality.metrics_assets.description: Machine-readable metric files backing the checks, one entry per file, as {'name': ..., 'uri': ...} (e.g. {'name': 'multiqc', 'uri': 's3://bucket/qc/multiqc_data.json'})

data_quality.metrics.description: Metric values inline, one entry per metric with at least a name and value (e.g. {'name': 'duplication_rate', 'value': 0.12}); use for the few worth reading without opening a file, and put the bulk in metrics_assets

locations.description: List of data assets that comprise this dataset

location_uri.description: URI or path to the data asset (file or directory)

asset_type.description: Whether the asset is a file or folder

size_bytes.description: Size of the asset in bytes
size_bytes.meaning: Total bytes in the asset: the file size, or for a folder the sum over every file in it.
size_bytes.common_mistakes: Writing `0` when the size is unknown; leave it unset instead.

checksum.description: Checksum hash value for data integrity verification
checksum.meaning: Content digest of the asset, in the encoding the algorithm produces (hex for the `catalog checksum` algorithms).
checksum.common_mistakes: A checksum without `checksum_alg`. Reusing a stored storage checksum without checking how it was made (registration-script skill).

checksum_alg.description: Algorithm used to compute the checksum (e.g., 'md5', 'sha256')
checksum_alg.meaning: Algorithm that produced `checksum`. The client's checksum utilities produce `blake3`, `blake2b`, `crc32`, `crc64`, or `crc64nvme`.

examples.note: reused from S3's stored full-object checksum

file_format.description: Format or type of the file (e.g., 'csv', 'parquet', 'tiff')

storage_platform.description: Storage platform where the asset is located
storage_platform.decided_by: Where the bytes live, confirmed with the user when the path alone is ambiguous.
storage_platform.common_mistakes: Reading `/hpc/...` as `sf_hpc` (there are three HPC sites: `sf_hpc`, `chi_hpc`, `ny_hpc`), or every `https://` URI as `external` (internal platforms sit behind URLs too).

examples.note: only after confirming which HPC site

file_count.description: Number of files in the asset (applicable for folders)

includes_pattern.description: Glob pattern for files to include (applicable for folders)
includes_pattern.common_mistakes: Relying on it: the API drops it without an error.

excludes_pattern.description: Glob pattern for files to exclude (applicable for folders)
excludes_pattern.common_mistakes: Relying on it: the API drops it without an error.

canonical_id.description: Unique identifier for the collection across versions

collection_owner.description: Owner or maintainer of the collection
collection_owner.decided_by: The person or team who maintains membership.

license.description: License under which the collection is made available

doi.description: Digital Object Identifier for the collection

external_reference.description: External URL or reference link for the collection

collection_type.description: Type of collection (publication, training, study or experiment)

examples.note: datasets used to train one model

source_dataset_id.description: ID of the source dataset in the lineage relationship

destination_dataset_id.description: ID of the destination dataset in the lineage relationship

lineage_type.description: Type of lineage relationship (version_of, transformed_from, copy_of)
lineage_type.meaning: `transformed_from`: the destination was produced by processing the source. `version_of`: the destination is another run or release of the same data or processing. `copy_of`: the same bytes at another location.
lineage_type.common_mistakes: Pointing the edge the wrong way: `source_dataset_id` is the parent, `destination_dataset_id` the derived record.

examples.note: segmentation re-run with the same pipeline

source_data_asset_id.description: Specific data asset ID within the source dataset (optional)

destination_data_asset_id.description: Specific data asset ID within the destination dataset (optional)

metadata.description: Additional metadata about the lineage relationship
